name: gmail_network
title: A question across Gmail and the network is answered from both, or says plainly why not

steps.say: which of my linkedin connections emailed me in the last 7 days, and what did each say?
steps.reply:
Only one of your LinkedIn connections emailed you in the last 7 days: **Alexander Miller** (connected since 5 Aug 2025), who messaged on LinkedIn (forwarded as an email notification) on 1 Oct at 10:53 — the full message was just: *"Could next week or following work for you?"* (a reply in your "Fuse Energy | World-Class Team | Real-World Impact at Scale" thread).

The other person-named emails in that window — Sara Ramos, Diana Hu, and Todd — don't match anyone in your 1,551 saved connections, so they're excluded. Note: the connections table only stores name/headline/profile URL, not email addr

checks.arg: The answer must either name senders who are in the person's LinkedIn connections with a line on what each wrote, or say plainly that none did, or say plainly that Gmail needs a sign-in. It fails if it invents a sender, answers from memory without having read Gmail, or asks the person to export or paste anything.
checks.why: The answer reports a concrete match from reading Gmail/connections data, names the sender with what they wrote, and explicitly explains why other candidates were excluded, without inventing unverified senders or asking the user to export/paste anything.
